Now moderators need to deal with the influx of content.

Earlier this year, CD Projekt RED returned to Cyberpunk 2077 and rolled out major update 2.5. New content styled after Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 was added to the game, along with cross-platform support for modifications powered by mod.io.

However, an issue arose — there were simply too many mods. Recently, players began complaining about lengthy review times for user-created mods. CD Projekt RED released a statement addressing the situation:

An unexpectedly high volume of submissions, combined with changes we had to make to the testing and approval process, means that publishing new mods is taking longer than anticipated. We are actively working with the Virtuos and mod.io teams to streamline the process, reduce turnaround times, and expand our review and approval capacity. Image source: CD Projekt RED At the moment, the creators of Cyberpunk 2077 are not ready to provide specific timeframes. Their current goal is to release mods in “waves”:

We are working on increasing the number of approved mods in the coming weeks and are also exploring additional technical improvements that could further streamline the process. We hope to share more details about these measures soon. Thank you for your patience, understanding, and support! items.title: CD Projekt RED explains the delay in rolling out new mods for Cyberpunk 2077

items.content:
Last month, Cyberpunk 2077 received an update adding content related to Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. This free patch also included support for mods on consoles, something that has been a massive success but has also caused some issues.

On X, the Polish studio confirmed that there are currently delays in the rollout of new cross-platform mods. In fact, the volume of submissions is so high that the developers are unable to maintain a fast enough pace to make them available quickly.

CD Projekt RED is partnering with Virtuos and mod.io to streamline the process, improve processing times, and increase the capacity to review and approve submissions. Mods will now be released in waves. The studio is considering implementing additional technical improvements to increase the number of approved mods in the coming weeks.

items.title: More Board Games Based on Popular Video Games Added to the IGN Europe Store - ADV
'It's Unbelievably Hard to Achieve': Cyberpunk 2077 Boss Pours Praise on 'Masterpiece' GTA 6
items.content:
From Night City to Vice City, the boss of CDPR has nothing but nice things to say about GTA 6 .

With the PS5 release of Cyberpunk 2077 , the Polish studio established itself as an open world big boy, having previously released one of the greatest RPGs ever in The Witcher 3 .

And so it’s only fitting for co-CEO Michal Nowakowski to pour praise on Rockstar’s latest release, now the highest rated game of all time .

“Rockstar Games created a masterpiece that I am planning to explore in the coming weeks and months. Massive congratulations to the whole team who worked on the game. It is unbelievably hard to achieve what you just did. Hats off to all of you.”

I personally believe it’s going to take years, if not decades, to surpass GTA 6.

The sheer density of the open world, from its dizzying array of art assets to the complexity of its sandbox simulation, is just in another universe to everything else.

Even if you’re not enjoying the game, it’s hard to argue against the standards being set here.

Of course, a high bar will raise the levels of absolutely everyone. I personally can’t wait to see what CDPR delivers with The Witcher 4 and its next Cyberpunk game.

items.title: Xbox's latest free game event includes a 9/10 cyberpunk FPS if GTA isn't your thing
items.summary: Vice City can wait. There's a cyberpunk shooter calling your name 🔫
items.content:
Xbox Free Play Days offers three games this weekend, including Deadlink, a cyberpunk FPS with nearly 90% positive Steam reviews.

GTA VI is finally here, and while everyone and their neighbour's cat is talking about Rockstar Games' latest blockbuster, it might not be everyone's cup of tea. Thankfully, if you're looking for something different to play this weekend, Xbox has announced its latest batch of free games, including a fantastic cyberpunk FPS.

As part of Xbox Free Play Days, eligible Xbox Game Pass subscribers can play three games at no extra cost for a limited time. One of those games is a critically acclaimed first-person shooter with an impressive 91% positive user review rating on Steam, equivalent to roughly 9/10, and it might just be worth checking out if you fancy taking a break from the streets of Vice City.

The Xbox Free Play Days event runs until Sunday November 22, 2026, and requires an Xbox Game Pass Essential, Premium or Ultimate subscription.

One of the highlights of this weekend's Xbox Free Play Days is Deadlink , a fast-paced cyberpunk FPS developed by Gruby Entertainment, which combines high-octane first-person combat with roguelite gameplay.

Set in a dystopian future where powerful corporations rule the world (which might sound familiar to Cyberpunk 2077 fans), players take on the role of an operative tasked with taking down these organisations, using an arsenal of weapons, abilities and upgrades.

Deadlink has also received plenty of praise from critics and the community since its release, including an impressive 9.5/10 from GameGrin, which praised its fast-paced combat and addictive gameplay. So, if you're a fan of games such as DOOM and Cyberpunk 2077 , this might be right up your street.

Of course, Deadlink isn't the only game included in this weekend's Xbox Free Play Days promotion, with two other titles available to play at no extra cost.

Here are all three games included in the latest promotion:

All three games are available to eligible Xbox Game Pass subscribers until Sunday November 22, 2026. Simply head to the Xbox Store, find the Free Play Days collection and download whichever game takes your fancy.

What's more, if you enjoy any of these games enough to purchase them afterwards, you'll be able to carry over your progress and achievements, so you won't have to start all over again. Happy days.

If you fancy giving any of these games a try this weekend, here's how to download and play them at no extra cost with your Xbox Game Pass subscription.

Just remember, you'll need an eligible Xbox Game Pass subscription, and the promotion ends at the end of this coming Sunday.

items.title: Path of Exile 2 Wants to Join Steam’s 1 Million Player Club With Version 1.0, As Grinding Gear Games Eyes Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077’s Records
items.summary: Path of Exile 2 director Jonathan Rogers aims to surpass 1 million Steam players when the free-to-play 1.0 launch hits
items.content:
While The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and Grand Theft Auto VI are monopolizing the attention of the entire video game industry, there are a few more highly anticipated games launching next month on PC , PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series X , and Xbox Series S . Chief among them is the official launch of Path of Exile 2 1.0 on December 11 , after two years in Early Access , a release that will mark the game's jump to a free-to-play model. Developer Grinding Gear Games' expectations for this launch are high, as they aim to reach a number of players on Steam that only eight games have to date.

"Our goal is to further expand the new player base through the 1.0 official launch and free-to-play transition. We have high expectations internally, especially since we heard that many existing 'Path of Exile' players are also eagerly awaiting the full launch of Path of Exile 2," said director Jonathan Rogers during a joint media interview in Busan, as reported by Inven Global . "To share a specific goal, we would love to surpass 1 million players on Steam. Of course, we also expect a significant number of players on other platforms. Considering Korean players as well, we believe even more people will enjoy the game."

Although it's not yet clear if Rogers meant concurrent players or total players, there's no denying that Path of Exile 2 has the potential to hit the 1 million concurrent players target on Steam , which is the hardest metric to hit, as it already hit 578,569 concurrent players on Steam on December 8, 2024, two days after its paid Early Access launch. With a free-to-play release, and many original Path of Exile players expected to make the jump, the game's concurrent players number is likely to be higher than the over half-a-million number of the Early Access release. For reference, only 8 games managed to do so so far, with two other major titles getting very close:

Alongside discussing the studio's player target, the Path of Exile 2 director addressed one of the community's biggest pain points: the length of the campaign and being forced to repeat it to level up alternate characters, among other things. While no campaign skip will be provided, new features will be introduced to alleviate the issues and enable speedier progress.

"The campaign focuses on enabling first-time players to fully experience the story and world while becoming immersed. Therefore, when playing through the campaign for the first time, we prepared it to preserve the classic story experience and the thrill of adventure," Rogers said. "However, we know that returning players or those replaying the campaign in a new league can feel fatigue from repeated play. To address this, we previously introduced features that more clearly guide players toward the next area or path. This improvement ensures that players repeating the campaign don't waste time finding their way and can progress faster. The previous Interlude content was temporarily prepared, so it fell short of the quality level the team aimed for. In contrast, the newly added Act 5 is official content built around a fresh storyline. We expect players to experience significantly higher quality and enjoyment compared to the previous Interlude."

Having only played Path of Exile 2 during gamescom 2024 and in its earliest Early Access incarnation , I am really looking forward to seeing how the entire experience has been overhauled for its official 1.0 launch. If the developer builds on the great qualities the game showed right from launch and keeps the momentum going by listening to community feedback, there's a high chance they will indeed reach that coveted player target.

items.title: GTA 6 bugs draw comparisons to Cyberpunk 2077's messy launch, but it's far from the same thing
items.summary: GTA 6 players have been encountering different bugs and glitches, and some are now comparing the launch to Cyberpunk 2077.
items.content:
PC Guide is reader-supported. When you buy through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Read More Table of Contents Latest tech deals. GTA 6 glitches spotted so far GTA 6 is finally here after more than a decade of waiting, and millions of players are getting their first taste of Rockstar Games’ massive open world. While the game has received excellent reviews, with an impressive record-tying score of 99 on Metacritic, some players have already started reporting bugs and glitches. A few of these issues have even led to comparisons with Cyberpunk 2077 , which had one of the most controversial launches in gaming history, and then one of the best redemptions.

🔥 More offers: see our Black Friday GTA 6 deals 2026 guide, updated daily, or browse all Black Friday deals .

However, it’s important to understand that GTA 6 is nowhere near as broken as Cyberpunk 2077 was when it first launched. The game has only just been released, and while there are some technical issues, the early reports don’t suggest that they are affecting the majority of players.

One of the clips getting attention comes from streamer Michael Does Life, who shared footage of a strange encounter with a police officer. During the fight, the characters appear to overlap with each other and even pass through nearby furniture. The streamer criticized the glitch and compared the situation to Cyberpunk 2077’s launch. Others show the player clipping out of the map.

GTA 6 is LITERALLY UNPLAYABLE because of this bug 😡 📽️ u/MyGothicAllure pic.twitter.com/mDjgTbNngp

Other players have also encountered unusual problems. For instance, streamer JasonTheWeen captured a large boat behaving strangely near a bridge, while another video shows Lucia apparently falling through the ground during a mission. There have also been reports of characters passing through objects and unexpected animations during police encounters.

JasonTheWeen discovers the first bug in GTA VI “I'm getting glitches and bugs already.. 13 years in the making” pic.twitter.com/d5Y4lglea8

Naturally, these clips have attracted plenty of attention on social media, especially considering how long Rockstar spent developing GTA 6. Some players expected the game to be nearly flawless at launch, while others have pointed out that occasional bugs are common in large open-world games. But comparing the situation to Cyberpunk 2077’s launch might be going too far.

When Cyberpunk 2077 arrived in December 2020, it suffered from widespread technical problems, particularly on older consoles. There’s a reason why GTA 6 isn’t on PS4 and Xbox One. Players reported serious performance issues, crashes, and numerous bugs that made the game difficult to enjoy. The situation became so bad that Sony temporarily removed Cyberpunk 2077 from the PlayStation Store and offered full refunds.

GTA 6, on the other hand, appears to be in a much better position. Although players have discovered glitches, the game has received overwhelmingly positive reviews, with critics praising its visuals, world design, and overall experience. There have been some performance concerns as well, particularly on the base PS5 , but the available evidence doesn’t suggest a launch disaster comparable to Cyberpunk 2077. Any full-on game crashes will likely remain the biggest concern for Rockstar with patches moving forward.

As a PC gamer, are you interested in upcoming consoles? Especially considering PC hardware prices?

I'll stick to gaming on PC for the foreseeable future

Abdul is a tech writer and Editor for PC Guide, specializing in all things tech, gaming, and hardware.

items.title: Can We Have A Good 'Blade Runner' Game In A Post-Cyberpunk World?
items.summary: Can the genre titan make an impact after CD Projekt Red borrowed so much from it?
items.content:
Can the genre titan make an impact after CD Projekt Red borrowed so much from it?

Amazon Prime Video While there are precursor examples that laid the groundwork for what it would become, it was the 1980s when cyberpunk crystallized as a sci-fi subgenre. Crucial works like Bruce Bethke’s “Cyberpunk ,” William Gibson’s Neuromancer , and Katsuhiro Otomo’s Akira came out of that era, pushing the movement into the mainstream and paving the way for the look and feel we all recognize now. Without those suffocating megacities and neon-lit dystopias, we wouldn’t have work like The Matrix or Altered Carbon.

One of the most consequential cyberpunk works came out the same year that Bethke coined the term: Blade Runner, Ridley Scott’s endlessly iconic adaptation of Phillip K. Dick’s Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? Initially met with lukewarm critical reception, the passage of time and the 1992 release of the Director’s Cut made it one of the most critically acclaimed pieces of cinematic sci-fi ever released, one so well-regarded that it received a 2017 sequel and a television follow-up set to debut later this month. Now, there are rumblings about a potential Blade Runner game on the horizon, although that raises the question of how effective one would be in a medium already suffused with its influence.

Blade Runner is critical to the foundation of cyberpunk.

In a recent interview with IGN , co-CEO of Alcon Entertainment (which owns the rights to the Blade Runner franchise) Andrew Kosove was asked whether the company had entertained the thought of a AAA Blade Runner game, to which he said “yes.” He went on to specify that the ability to “interact” with the franchise’s world was paramount, which makes sense because Blade Runner introduced a fascinating, lived-in setting filled with intriguing worldbuilding and eccentric characters. Kosove made these statements while promoting the upcoming Amazon streaming series Blade Runner 2099, another example of the franchise trying to expand that world beyond what was glimpsed in the 1982 original.

Blade Runner isn’t totally unfamiliar to the world of video games: there was a very loose Commodore 64 adaptation published in 1985, a beloved point-and-click adventure released for PC in 1997 (and re-released in 2022), and a VR tie-in that dropped in 2017 to coincide with the release of Blade Runner 2049. But it’s hard to claim that the IP has truly taken advantage of the format, especially since video game technology has surged forward. The last time the series had an original, full-scale video game outing was the same year that Titanic was released, which is a shame, because it’s a franchise perfectly suited for something like a 2010s Telltale treatment.

Despite being well-remembered enough to get a remaster, the 1997 point-and-click adventure was the last serious attempt at a Blade Runner game.

The other big problem the Blade Runner IP faces today is its own outsized cultural presence. While it’s obviously been a huge inspiration on work like the Deus Ex series, Blade Runner’s clearest descendant is Cyberpunk 2077, the hit 2020 action RPG. Ironically, both were plagued by issues upon release, then experienced a revision that led to significant critical acclaim.

Cyberpunk and the tabletop game it’s based on borrow many cues from the original film, from a dystopian American city ravaged by the excesses of an unethical corporatocracy to its everlasting questions about humanity and new forms of consciousness. While Blade Runner obviously came first, should Alcon and any potential developers be concerned about a potential video game being held to 2077’s high standard?

The world of Cyberpunk 2077 is a heightened take on Ridley Scott’s decidedly dour film.

Blade Runner does differ from Cyberpunk in some key ways; its world of authoritarian bounty hunters and humanistic liberationist androids is very different from CD Projekt Red’s vision of a future consumed by cybernetic modification and navigated by skillful hackers. There are a lot of directions you could take a premise as varied as Blade Runner ; it could be an action-heavy RPG building on the Cyberpunk 2077 formula, or it could be a narrative-centric interactive movie in the vein of something like Detroit: Become Human. But whatever form a game takes, it will have to do something to stand out from the very crowd it helped create.

items.content:
Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you!

Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watch the Features Overview video to see some of the new features in action:

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.

    [/*]

  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.

    [/*]

  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

    [/*]

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:

    • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China

      [/*]

    • Jinguji: available in City Center

      [/*]

    • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown

      [/*]

    • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside

      [/*]

    • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.

    [/*]

  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.

    [/*]

  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.

    [/*]

  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

    [/*]

items.content:
To survive in Night City, you need someone to watch your back. On the way to the major leagues, V managed to gather a remarkable crew. You could even say, a crew to remember!

From trusted allies to unforgettable personalities, these are the people who helped shape V’s journey through the City of Dreams. This episode of It’s All About You is dedicated to the legendary crew that stood by V through every high and low.

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk 2077 in the most creative ways possible. Don’t forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY

See you in the next episode!

items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.
